title: GNSS-disciplined clock holdover per oscillator grade, and a slow time-walk spoof
summary: A stdlib-only simulation of a GNSS-disciplined oscillator (type-2 PLL on a noisy 1PPS) for TCXO, OCXO, rubidium and chip-scale atomic clock grades, with ADEV, aging and temperature figures taken from Vig's oscillator comparison table and the Microchip SA65 datasheet. It reports time error after 1 min to 24 h of GNSS outage (Monte Carlo median and 95th percentile, next to an analytic estimate), then walks GNSS time off slowly and compares an internal steering-plausibility monitor with a cross-check against a second time source, including a guard that drops into holdover on alarm and no-spoof control runs.
verified: ran with python3.14.7 stdlib on 2026-11-06 (default arguments, about 5 s); output pasted verbatim in README. 9 unittest tests pass, including an ADEV check of the noise model, a no-spoof negative control and a planted blind-detector control that proves the cross-source alarm can fail. Oscillator parameters are datasheet/table values; PPS noise, second-source noise/asymmetry, temperature fraction and detector thresholds are stated assumptions. No hardware or real GNSS data was used, and none of the related repos was run.
